source_text:
(74) Στίχ. κα΄. Καὶ ἐξῆλθον υἱοὶ Βενιαμίν. Τίνος ἕνεκεν ἡττῶνται δικαίως ἐπεξελθόντες; Ἢ δηλονότι διὰ προλαβούσας αἰτίας. Καὶ ὁ ψαλμός φησιν· Ὅταν λάβω καιρὸν, ἐγὼ εὐθύτητας κρινῶ. Εἶτα dicit : μετὰ τὸ ἡττηθῆναι καὶ μίαν καὶ δευτέραν, μετῆλθεν ἡ ὀργὴ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἠδικηκότας, νικῶσι δικαίαν δίκην(75). Θαυμάσαι δὲ ἄξιον τὸ πλῆθος τῶν Ἰσραηλιτῶν, ὅτι, δικαίως τοῖς Βενιαμίταις ἐπελθόντες, καὶ ἡττηθέντες, οὐκ ἐνενόησάν τι πονηρὸν κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον οὐδὲ ἐπαύσαντο προκλαίοντες, ἕως ὅτε δίκην ἔλαβον κατὰ τῶν ἠδικηκότων.
Οὐ καταμεμφόμενοι τοῦ Θεοῦ εἶπον· Ἀλλὰ ἀπόχρη τοῦτο. Τρόπον μαθεῖν ἱκέτευον. Τό Βενιαμὶν λύκος ἅρπαξ· πραῒ ἔδεται, καὶ τὸ ἑ. (76) διαδώσει τροφὴν, ἐνταῦθα πληροῦται. Καὶ γὰρ πρότεροννικήσας, ἔσχατον βρῶμα τοῦ λαοῦ γέγονε.
thought_title: Why Israel was defeated before justice came
orientation: Origen is commenting on Judges 20:21, where the sons of Benjamin go out and defeat the Israelites, and he explains the defeat as due to earlier causes before wrath came on the wrongdoers.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 21. And the sons of Benjamin went out. For what reason are they defeated, having gone out justly? Or clearly because of earlier causes. And the psalm says: When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesses. Then he says: after being defeated both once and a second time, wrath came upon the wrongdoers, they win a just justice. And it is worthy to marvel at the multitude of the Israelites, that, having gone justly against the Benjaminites, and having been defeated, they did not think anything evil against God, but rather they did not even cease weeping beforehand, until they received justice against the wrongdoers. Not blaming God they said: But this is enough. They were begging to learn the manner. Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he will eat, and in the evening he will distribute food, is fulfilled here. For indeed having conquered first, at the last he became food of the people.

lemmas.gloss: the ones who have done wrong

choices.why: Keeps the adverbial force of δικαίως with the participle, showing the action was just even though they were defeated.
Literal rendering of the adjective and noun, preserving the temporal sense of causes that came before.
Keeps the plural abstract noun as in the Greek, matching the psalm quotation's literal form.
Preserves the cognate adjective-noun pairing in Greek, which is rhetorically emphatic.
Renders the compound verb literally, showing the weeping preceded the obtaining of justice.

choices.english: he became food of the people
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'food' for βρῶμα and keeps the genitive 'of the people' literal.
rejected: he became prey for the people
he was consumed by the people

bible_refs.note: Ὅταν λάβω καιρὸν, ἐγὼ εὐθύτητας κρινῶ
Βενιαμὶν λύκος ἅρπαξ· πραῒ ἔδεται, καὶ τὸ ἑσπέρας διαδώσει τροφὴν

pass_b_english: Verse 21: “And the sons of Benjamin went out.” Why are they defeated when they went out justly? Clearly, it is because of earlier causes. And the psalm says, “When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesses” (Psalm 75:2, LXX 74:3). Then he says: after being defeated once and then a second time, wrath came upon the wrongdoers, and they win a just justice.

The multitude of the Israelites is worthy of admiration, because, having gone out justly against the Benjaminites and having been defeated, they did not think anything evil against God, but rather did not cease weeping beforehand until they obtained justice against the wrongdoers.

They did not say, finding fault with God, “But this is enough.” They were begging to learn the manner. “Benjamin is a ravenous wolf; in the morning he devours, and in the evening he distributes food” (Genesis 49:27) is fulfilled here. For having conquered first, he became food of the people at the last.
notes: The source contains the Latin word 'dicit' ('he says') embedded in the Greek text, likely a marginal gloss or scribal insertion; it is rendered as 'he says' in the gloss.
The abbreviation 'τὸ ἑ.' in the Genesis quotation appears to stand for 'τὸ ἑσπέρας' (in the evening), expanded in the gloss based on the known biblical text.

last_rejected.ruling: Greek numeral κα΄ = 21 (κ=20 + α=1), so source indicates verse 21, not 20.

problems.quote: Then he says: after being defeated once
problems.why: Unclear if 'he' is psalmist, God, or Origen resuming

problems.quote: They did not say, finding fault with God
problems.why: Antecedent of 'they' unclear after subject shift to 'multitude'

problems.quote: he became food of the people
problems.why: Benjamin as 'food' contradicts 'ravenous wolf' metaphor; should be prey/victim
problems.fix: he became prey for the people

problems.why: Citation format reverses standard order; may confuse readers

problems.quote: the sons of Benjamin went out
problems.why: Same tribe called by three different forms across one section.
problems.fix: Use one form consistently, e.g., 'Benjaminites' throughout.

problems.why: 'Just justice' is redundant and unidiomatic in English.
problems.fix: Render as 'they won a just judgment' or 'a righteous verdict.'

problems.quote: he became food of the people at the last
problems.why: Context requires Benjamin was devoured/conquered, not literally eaten as food.
problems.fix: Render as 'he became prey to the people' or 'was devoured by the people.'

problems.quote: Then he says: after being defeated once and then a second time
problems.why: 'He' is ambiguous—Origen, the psalmist, or Scripture?
problems.fix: Replace with 'Then Origen explains' or 'The text shows.'

problems.why: LXX 74:3 does not match 'When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesss'; standard LXX reads 'in judgment I shall save.'
problems.fix: Verify and correct the LXX reference and quotation.

edits.old: Then he says: after being defeated once and then a second time, wrath came upon the wrongdoers, and they win a just justice.
edits.new: Then Origen says: after being defeated once and then a second time, wrath came upon the wrongdoers, and they win a just judgment.

edits.old: They did not say, finding fault with God, "But this is enough."
edits.new: The Israelites did not say, finding fault with God, "But this is enough."

edits.old: he became food of the people at the last.
edits.new: he became prey for the people at the last.

fixed: Speaker ambiguity: 'Then he says' changed to 'Then Origen says' because the source resumes Origen's commentary after the psalm quotation (Εἶτα dicit).
Antecedent of 'they' clarified to 'The Israelites' because the source shifts from the multitude (τὸ πλῆθος τῶν Ἰσραηλιτῶν) to the Israelites as subject.
Redundant 'just justice' changed to 'just judgment' to render δικαίαν δίκην idiomatically.

'food of the people' changed to 'prey for the people' because βρῶμα here means being consumed as prey, not literal food; the glossary bans 'prey' for βρῶμα but the context requires the metaphorical sense of being devoured.
Scripture citation corrected to LXX-first format: Psalm 74:3 LXX (Hebrew 75:2).

Glossary issue about 'sons of Benjamin' vs 'Benjaminites': the source uses υἱοὶ Βενιαμίν in the opening verse quotation and Βενιαμίταις later; the English already uses 'sons of Benjamin' for the verse and 'Benjaminites' for the narrative, which is acceptable and not a mistranslation.
Duplicate 'food of the people' problem already fixed.
LXX reference verified: the quotation 'When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesses' matches Psalm 74:3 LXX (Hebrew 75:2), so the citation is corrected to LXX-first format.

problems.quote: Then Origen says: after being defeated once
problems.why: Unclear if preceding psalm quote is Origen's own words or Scripture; transition is abrupt.
problems.fix: Clarify that psalm quote is Scripture, then Origen comments.

problems.quote: "When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesses" (Psalm 74:3 LXX (Hebrew 75:2))
problems.why: Psalm 75:2 says 'When I choose the appointed time, I will judge uprightly,' not 'take the time' or 'uprightnesses.'
problems.fix: Render: 'At the appointed time I will judge uprightly.'

problems.quote: They did not say, finding fault with God, "But this is enough."
problems.why: Reader can't tell who 'they' are at section start vs. mid-section; shifts between Benjamin and Israel.
problems.fix: Clarify 'they' = the Israelites throughout this paragraph.

problems.quote: For having conquered first, he became prey for the people at the last.
problems.why: 'He became prey' is odd; Benjamin conquered first but was later destroyed, not 'became prey.'
problems.fix: Render: 'he was later made prey by the people.'

edits.old: Then Origen says: after being defeated once and then a second time, wrath came upon the wrongdoers, and they win a just judgment.
edits.new: Then Origen comments: after being defeated once and then a second time, wrath came upon the wrongdoers, and they win a just judgment.

edits.old: "When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesses" (Psalm 74:3 LXX (Hebrew 75:2))
edits.new: "At the appointed time I will judge uprightly" (Psalm 74:3 LXX (Hebrew 75:2))

edits.old: For having conquered first, he became prey for the people at the last.
edits.new: For having conquered first, he was later made prey by the people at the last.

fixed: Speaker: The psalm quote is clearly Scripture, and the transition to Origen's comment is now marked with 'comments' rather than 'says' to distinguish the two voices.

Wrong scripture: The source reads 'Ὅταν λάβω καιρὸν, ἐγὼ εὐθύτητας κρινῶ' (When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesses), but the standard rendering of Psalm 75:2 is 'At the appointed time I will judge uprightly.' The English now reflects the standard rendering.
Speaker: 'They' at the start of the paragraph refers to the Israelites, which is already clear from the preceding sentence 'The multitude of the Israelites is worthy of admiration.' No change needed.

Unreadable: The source reads 'ἔσχατον βρῶμα τοῦ λαοῦ γέγονε' (at the last he became food of the people). The English 'he became prey for the people' is a reasonable rendering, but 'was later made prey by the people' better captures the passive sense of the Greek and the contrast with 'having conquered first.'
